listing.name: Tip Calculator & Bill Splitter
listing.description: Work out the tip and split the bill between any number of people, with tip on the pre-tax amount and rounding up per person.
listing.shortDescription: Tip amount, total and each person’s share, with preset or custom tip percentages.

title: Tip Calculator: Split the Bill & Tip Per Person
description: Work out the tip and split the bill between any number of people. Preset or custom tip %, tip on the pre-tax amount, and round each share up.
quickAnswer: Tip = bill × tip % ÷ 100, total = bill + tip, and each person pays total ÷ number of people. An 85.50 bill with an 18% tip is 15.39 in tip and 100.89 in total, so three people pay 33.63 each. To tip only on the food and drink, take the tax out of the bill first.

formula.title: Tip and Split Formula
formula.expression: Tip = Bill × Tip% ÷ 100   ·   Total = Bill + Tip   ·   Per person = Total ÷ People
formula.explanation: The tip is rounded to the nearest cent, added to the bill, and the total is divided between the people sharing it. If the total does not divide evenly, the calculator says how many people pay one extra cent so the shares add up exactly. With tip on pre-tax amount switched on, the tax is backed out of the bill first: pre-tax amount = bill ÷ (1 + tax% ÷ 100), and the tip is worked out on that amount only.

commonMistakes.title: Tipping on a service charge that is already included
commonMistakes.description: Some restaurants add a service charge or gratuity to the bill, often for larger groups. Check the receipt before adding a tip on top, or you may tip twice.

commonMistakes.title: Splitting the bill before adding the tip
commonMistakes.description: If everyone divides the food bill and then rounds their own tip, the total tip is often less than intended. Add the tip to the whole bill first, then split the total.

commonMistakes.title: Rounding every share down
commonMistakes.description: Rounding 33.63 down to 33 for three people leaves the table 1.89 short. Round shares up, or use the exact amount and let the calculator assign the odd cents.

commonMistakes.title: Assuming the same tipping custom everywhere
commonMistakes.description: Whether a tip is expected, and how much, varies by country, by type of business and even by city. When travelling, check local guidance or ask; in some places service is included in prices.

commonMistakes.title: Forgetting tax when tipping on the subtotal
commonMistakes.description: If you want to tip on the pre-tax amount, use the subtotal from the receipt or turn on the pre-tax option and enter the tax rate, rather than tipping on the bill total.

howto.name: How to Calculate a Tip and Split the Bill
howto.description: Work out the tip, the total and what each person owes.

steps.name: Enter the bill
steps.text: Type the amount on the receipt and choose your currency.

steps.name: Choose the tip
steps.text: Pick 10, 15, 18, 20 or 25%, or type any percentage.

steps.name: Enter the number of people
steps.text: Enter how many people are sharing the bill.

steps.name: Adjust the options
steps.text: Tip on the pre-tax amount if you prefer, and round each share up to a whole amount if that is easier to pay.

faqs.q: How do I calculate a tip?
faqs.a: Multiply the bill by the tip percentage and divide by 100. For a 60 bill and a 15% tip: 60 × 15 ÷ 100 = 9, so the total is 69. A quick mental trick for 20% is to move the decimal point one place left and double it.

faqs.q: How do you split a bill with tip between people?
faqs.a: Add the tip to the bill to get the total, then divide by the number of people. If it does not divide evenly to the cent, some people pay one cent more; the calculator tells you how many.
18% of 85.50 is 15.39. The total with tip is 100.89, which is 33.63 each for three people.

faqs.q: Should I tip on the total before or after tax?
faqs.a: Etiquette guides differ. Many people tip on the pre-tax subtotal because tax is not part of the service. Switch on 'Tip on the pre-tax amount' and enter the tax rate to see both figures.
It depends on where you are and the type of service. Customs range from no tip at all to a set percentage. Choose a preset or type your own percentage; the calculator does not assume a country.

faqs.q: What does round up per person do?
faqs.a: It rounds each share up to the next whole unit (for example 33.63 to 34.00). The extra cents go to the tip, and the result shows the tip percentage you are actually leaving.

faqs.q: Is a service charge the same as a tip?
faqs.a: Not always. A service charge is added by the business and may be shared differently from a voluntary tip. Rules on who receives service charges and tips vary by country, so check local guidance.

tipping-customs-differ.heading: Tipping Customs Differ
tipping-customs-differ.p1: There is no single rule for tipping. In some countries a tip is a large part of a server's income and is expected; in others service is included in menu prices or a service charge appears on the bill, and a tip is only a small extra for good service. Hotels, taxis, delivery and hairdressers often have their own customs. Because these customs vary and change, this calculator does not suggest a percentage for any country. Check local guidance when travelling, and look at the receipt for a service charge before adding a tip.
tipping-customs-differ.p2: Employment rules on tips also vary. In the United States, the Department of Labor sets rules for tipped employees and tip pools, and the IRS treats tips as taxable income for the worker. In the UK, employers must pass all tips, gratuities and service charges to workers without deductions. The sources below link to these official pages.

splitting-fairly.heading: Splitting Fairly
splitting-fairly.li1: Even split: best when everyone ordered similar amounts. The calculator divides to the cent and tells you if anyone needs to pay a cent more.
splitting-fairly.li2: Itemised split: if orders differ a lot, run the calculator once per person with their own subtotal and a single person count, using the same tip percentage.
splitting-fairly.li3: Paying in cash: turn on rounding up so everyone puts in a whole amount; the extra is added to the tip.
